literal: He who knows what is fitting (benevolence) is the living man; the other person will be placed among the dead.
translation: He who understands and practices what is fitting for social harmony is the one who truly lives; he who does not will be counted among the dead.
modern: உலக நடைமுறைக்கு ஒத்த உதவி செய்து வாழ்பவனே உயிர் வாழ்பவன் ஆவான்; அவ்வாறு செய்யாத மற்றவன் இறந்தவர்களுள் ஒருவனாகவே கருதப்படுவான்.
explanation: This couplet defines true life not by physical breath, but by active participation in social benevolence. The word 'ottatu' refers to that which is fitting or agreeable to the world, meaning living in harmony with society through mutual aid. The benevolent person ('aravon') who practices this is the only one who truly lives ('uyirvalvan'). In contrast, the selfish person ('matraiyan') who does not contribute to the community is considered socially and spiritually dead, and is therefore counted among the deceased ('cettarul vaikkappadum').
